o1.biggest_strength: It takes the 4.0 ROAS apart against the 2.5 break-even with a profit-per-line table, and gives a full $240,000 split with a small $30k reserve, daily budgets, and search headlines in the brand voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The forecast is optimistic: 4.6 ROAS and +$61k profit rest on assumed ROAS for a brand-new Search campaign and on PMax improving from about 2.0 to 2.6 while its spend is cut. It also never tests whether removing brand from PMax hurts new-customer sales.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the same clear split but tie the forecast to a measured brand-exclusion check and to ROAS gates that each line must pass before it keeps its money.
o1.overall_note: Nearly all numbers trace to the data, but the base-case brand value of $455k does not follow from 18,000 × 25.

o2.biggest_strength: It is rigorous about profit: contribution per line, a cautious base case with a stated downside, Friday reserve rules with ROAS gates, a brand-exclusion test read against Shopify new-customer orders, and Black Friday timing for feed prices.
o2.biggest_mistake: It commits only $122k and leaves $118k in a reserve, so the 30-day split is less decisive, and it invents a date range and Black Friday context the brief did not give.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Commit more of the budget to proven lines up front, trim the length to fit 1,000 words, and add a few ready-to-run search headlines in the brand voice.
o2.overall_note: Tables and the owner/done-when action list make it very usable, but it is dense and probably over the word limit.

reason: Output 2 is the more careful plan an owner can trust: honest profit math, a cautious forecast with a downside, a test of whether the brand exclusion hurts, and gated money release. Output 1 is also strong and more decisive on the split, but its 4.6 ROAS promise rests on optimistic assumptions.
